```{r}
## Assignment 5
## Step 2: How to use the GovInfo API
## Documentation: https://api.govinfo.gov/docs

library(httr2)

## Collections: see what is available

collections <- request("https://api.govinfo.gov/collections") |>
  req_url_query(api_key = Sys.getenv("GOVINFO_API_KEY")) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

# Print the list of collections
collections$collections
```

```{r}
## CHRG: Congressional Hearings
## Documents added or changed since the specified date

hearings <- request(
  "https://api.govinfo.gov/collections/CHRG/2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
) |>
  req_url_query(
    api_key = Sys.getenv("GOVINFO_API_KEY"),
    pageSize = 100,
    offsetMark = "*"
  ) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

# Inspect the first package
hearings$packages[[1]]
```

```{r}
## Search: Senate Committee on Foreign Relations
## Sort by publication date, newest first

body <- list(
  query       = 'collection:(CHRG) AND "Committee on Foreign Relations"',
  pageSize    = 100,
  offsetMark  = "*",
  sorts       = list(list(field = "publishdate", sortOrder = "DESC"))
)

found <- request("https://api.govinfo.gov/search") |>
  req_url_query(api_key = Sys.getenv("GOVINFO_API_KEY")) |>
  req_body_json(body) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

# Number of matching results
found$count

# Inspect the first result
found$results[[1]]



## Extract the list of search results
## Select simple fields from each document

govfiles <- lapply(found$results, function(x) {
  data.frame(
    packageId = if (is.null(x$packageId)) NA_character_ else x$packageId,
    title = if (is.null(x$title)) NA_character_ else x$title,
    dateIssued = if (is.null(x$dateIssued)) NA_character_ else x$dateIssued,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()

# View the first ten results
head(govfiles, 10)
```

```{r}
## Assignment 5

library(purrr)
library(magrittr)

## Set the working directory

setwd("D:/PhD in Political Science-UTD/Fall 2026/Methods of Data Collection and Production/avinash13808138.github.io")

## CSV method

govfiles = read.csv(
  file = "govinfo-search-results-2026-10-12T17_20_48.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

## Keep the first ten unique hearings
## The CSV was exported with Date (New to Old)

govfiles_csv <- govfiles[!duplicated(govfiles$packageId), ]

govfiles_csv[, c("packageId", "title", "publishdate")]
```

```{r}
## Directories to save the PDFs

dir.create("govinfo_pdfs", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("govinfo_pdfs/csv", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("govinfo_pdfs/api", showWarnings = FALSE)

## Exclude the PDF folder from the public repository

ignore_lines <- if (file.exists(".gitignore")) {
  readLines(".gitignore", warn = FALSE)
} else {
  character()
}

if (!("govinfo_pdfs/" %in% ignore_lines)) {
  cat("\ngovinfo_pdfs/\n", file = ".gitignore", append = TRUE)
}


## Function to download PDFs

download_govfiles_pdf <- function(url, id) {
  tryCatch({
    destfile <- paste0(save_dir, "govfiles_", id, ".pdf")

    status <- download.file(
      url,
      destfile = destfile,
      mode = "wb"
    )

    if (status != 0) {
      stop("Download failed")
    }

    # Check that the downloaded file has a PDF header
    pdf_header <- readBin(destfile, what = "raw", n = 5)

    if (!identical(pdf_header, charToRaw("%PDF-"))) {
      stop("Downloaded file is not a PDF")
    }

    Sys.sleep(runif(1, 1, 3))

    return(paste("Successfully downloaded:", id))
  },
  error = function(e) {
    return(paste("Failed to download:", id))
  })
}


## Prepare the CSV download list

pdf_govfiles_url <- govfiles_csv$pdfLink
pdf_govfiles_id <- govfiles_csv$packageId

save_dir <- "govinfo_pdfs/csv/"

## Download ten documents

start.time <- Sys.time()
message("Starting CSV downloads")

results_csv <- 1:10 %>%
  purrr::map_chr(
    ~ download_govfiles_pdf(
      pdf_govfiles_url[.],
      pdf_govfiles_id[.]
    )
  )

message("Finished CSV downloads")
end.time <- Sys.time()
time.taken <- end.time - start.time

time.taken
print(results_csv)

## Save the CSV download log

log_csv <- data.frame(
  method = "CSV export",
  packageId = govfiles_csv$packageId,
  title = govfiles_csv$title,
  pdfLink = govfiles_csv$pdfLink,
  result = results_csv,
  downloaded_at = as.character(end.time)
)

write.csv(
  log_csv,
  "govinfo_download_log_csv.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)




## API method

body <- list(
  query = 'collection:(CHRG) AND chamber:senate AND committee:"Foreign Relations"',
  pageSize = 100,
  offsetMark = "*",
  sorts = list(list(field = "publishdate", sortOrder = "DESC"))
)

found <- request("https://api.govinfo.gov/search") |>
  req_url_query(api_key = Sys.getenv("GOVINFO_API_KEY")) |>
  req_body_json(body) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

## Extract simple fields from the API results
## This avoids the earlier nested-list error

govfiles_api <- lapply(found$results, function(x) {
  data.frame(
    packageId = x$packageId,
    granuleId = if (is.null(x$granuleId) ||
                    length(x$granuleId) == 0 ||
                    !nzchar(x$granuleId)) {
      x$packageId
    } else {
      x$granuleId
    },
    title = x$title,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()

## Keep the first ten unique hearings

govfiles_api <- govfiles_api[
  !duplicated(govfiles_api$packageId),
]

govfiles_api <- head(govfiles_api, 10)

stopifnot(nrow(govfiles_api) == 10)

# Print the selected hearings
govfiles_api


## Prepare PDF links from API identifiers

govfiles_api$pdfLink <- paste0(
  "https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/",
  govfiles_api$packageId,
  "/pdf/",
  govfiles_api$granuleId,
  ".pdf"
)

pdf_govfiles_url <- govfiles_api$pdfLink
pdf_govfiles_id <- govfiles_api$packageId

save_dir <- "govinfo_pdfs/api/"

## Download ten documents

start.time <- Sys.time()
message("Starting API downloads")

results_api <- 1:10 %>%
  purrr::map_chr(
    ~ download_govfiles_pdf(
      pdf_govfiles_url[.],
      pdf_govfiles_id[.]
    )
  )

message("Finished API downloads")
end.time <- Sys.time()
time.taken <- end.time - start.time

time.taken
print(results_api)

## Save the API download log

log_api <- data.frame(
  method = "GovInfo API",
  packageId = govfiles_api$packageId,
  title = govfiles_api$title,
  pdfLink = govfiles_api$pdfLink,
  result = results_api,
  downloaded_at = as.character(end.time)
)

write.csv(
  log_api,
  "govinfo_download_log_api.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)



## Create the CSV log from the Step 4 download results
## No need to download the PDFs again

log_csv <- data.frame(
  method = "CSV export",
  packageId = govfiles_csv$packageId,
  title = govfiles_csv$title,
  pdfLink = govfiles_csv$pdfLink,
  result = results_csv,
  downloaded_at = NA_character_
)

## Save the CSV log

write.csv(
  log_csv,
  "govinfo_download_log_csv.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

## Combine both download logs

download_log <- rbind(log_csv, log_api)

write.csv(
  download_log,
  "govinfo_download_log.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# View the combined log
download_log

## Combine both download logs

download_log <- rbind(log_csv, log_api)

write.csv(
  download_log,
  "govinfo_download_log.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)



## Same ten hearings, regardless of order?

setequal(
  govfiles_csv$packageId,
  govfiles_api$packageId
)

## Same ten hearings in the same order?

identical(
  govfiles_csv$packageId,
  govfiles_api$packageId
)

## Hearings found only in the CSV list

setdiff(
  govfiles_csv$packageId,
  govfiles_api$packageId
)

## Hearings found only in the API list

setdiff(
  govfiles_api$packageId,
  govfiles_csv$packageId
)

## Count successful downloads
## Expected: 10 for each method

sum(grepl("^Successfully downloaded:", results_csv))
sum(grepl("^Successfully downloaded:", results_api))
```

## Step 4 : Report

### Difficulties encountered

I downloaded the ten most recent Senate Committee on Foreign Relations hearings available through the refined GovInfo search, including subcommittee hearings, using both a website CSV export and API search results. Both methods successfully downloaded ten PDFs and returned the same ten hearings in the same order.

The initial phrase search also returned a hearing issued by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation because it mentioned Foreign Relations. I addressed this by restricting the search to the Senate chamber and the Foreign Relations committee. I also encountered an R error when combining API results because some fields contained nested lists of unequal lengths. Extracting simple fields before combining the records resolved this problem. Another error occurred when combining download logs before the CSV log object had been created; creating the missing log resolved it.

### a. Usability of the documents as data

The PDFs provide source documents for analysis, but downloading them does not automatically produce an analysis-ready dataset. Their text must first be extracted and checked for completeness. Any scanned pages without usable embedded text would require optical character recognition (OCR). Headers, footers, page numbers, and formatting may also require cleaning, while tables and images may need separate processing.

To create a document-level table, I would use one row per hearing and include its package ID, title, date, committee, and document link. To create a text corpus, I would extract each hearing’s text, associate it with its package ID, and check the extraction against the original PDF. Analysis of individual statements would require additional work to identify speakers and separate their testimony.

### b. Improvements to the process

I would use committee and chamber metadata filters from the beginning rather than relying only on a phrase search. I would also examine the available HTML or text versions before extracting text from PDFs, since these formats may simplify text processing. The PDFs would remain useful for checking the original layout, tables, and images.

Metadata can supply identifiers, titles, dates, committee information, and available download links without manually opening each hearing. I would preserve this metadata alongside the download log, record the query and sorting settings, and add retries for failed requests. If collecting more documents, I would use pagination to retrieve additional results.

### c. What the API added

The API provided structured search results and document metadata that R could retrieve directly, reducing the manual exporting and page parsing required by website searches and scraping. It also supported repeatable requests with specified queries, sorting, and pagination, making the collection process easier to document and rerun.
